newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia, Slovenia plan nuclear plant joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Croatia, Slovenia plan nuclear plant joint venture.

text.p: Croatia and Slovenia are close to signing a deal on the joint ownership and management of Slovenia's only nuclear plant, the Croatian daily Vjesnik reported on Wednesday.
It quoted deputy economy minister in charge of energy, Zeljko Lalic, as saying that a new inter-government agreement had been prepared and was ready to be signed by July 1.
According to the deal, the plant would be set up as a limited liability company in which both states would have an equal share.
The company is not expected to make profit, and each side would cover its half of the costs.
Croatia and Slovenia each named four members to the joint supervisory board, due to meet beginning of May.

The issue of ownership and management of the Krsko nuclear plant was among outstanding problems that marred the relations between the two countries since they declared independence from former Yugoslavia in June 1991.
The plant was built jointly by the two states on the Slovenian side of the border while they were still part of the federation.
It produced 4.37 million megawat hours of electric power in 1996, and 1.2 million in the first three months of this year.
The plant is due for a regular annual overhaul from May 9 to June 12, Lalic said, adding that no electricity shortages were expected.
